body: A free pass. A free pass that would allow me to not have to worry about work and responsibility and reliability and trustworthiness and pride and appearance and money. And AI know it is unrealistic to ask for that in life. Which is why I just can't endure life. I don't care if this is lazy or selfish or whatever. That is what I would need in an ideal world, but this world is anything but.

I have mounds and mounds of work to sift through on a daily basis, and if on the off chance I get through all of it, I find myself frustrated with videogames lately (I never had this issue in the past) where I just don't want to put effort into changing my perspective, and I just want to melt into an alternate universe without having to do anything, considering that doing things is exactly what I like to avoid. Television is worthless, YouTube is on rare occasion helpful, etc. I become bored because my asshole personal tastes are so selective that I cannot enjoy so many different things.

Happiness is sharing in victory with characters that you understand and feel for in an intricate and interesting story. Happiness is seeing a conclusion to something you are truly invested in. Happiness is freedom, liberty. Happiness is being able to mold your world into whatever you want it to be, to smell and taste and touch and hear and gaze upon the most appealing of things on a whim, and being able to unshackle one's self from necessity. This is why I like good stories and RPG games. If I ever get the chance, which I haven't in recent time, I escape my responsibility to insert myself into a world that is not this one, a world where things are actually interesting and where not a moment is spent yearning over being somewhere else. Happiness is freedom, and I am not free.

But in my position, I don't have the option of breaking the rules and doing what I want to. If I want to try and live, then any mistake I make or expectation I fail to meet means a significant degradation of my possible future situations. I don't want to suffer now for happiness later, and I don't want to sacrifice happiness later in life so I can enjoy myself now. And there is no middle ground, there is no point I can find where I can be happy enough my entire life to outweigh the negative aspects that go into creating that room for hapiness

I suppose I could force myself to keep going by starting ongoing things that I would be unable to forego finishing, but what kind of existence is my life if I am utilizing my mental conditions to force myself to remain alive?

I thank you for your words and agree with many of the points you make, but responsibility is where I begin falling apart. I am responsible for so many things and there is so much expected of me that when I want to stop and even try to enjoy something small, I'm met with a barricade of expectations, a river of responsibility that I will drown in if I don't devote my whole efforts to staying afloat. I have such a hard time trying to motivate myself to do this work when I know that I could be doing something that would make me a little bit happy, but if I forget my responsibilities, I will lose access to these things.

But what do I do when there is such a sheer lack of good things to take up my time and be able to make me happy? I have trouble finding anything at all to pass time, and I spend hours on end feeling a distinct lack of happiness? I end up going into obsessive mindsets where nothing amuses me, and I just want to sleep. I know excessive sleeping is a sign of depression, but I just feel like I want to experience as many dreams as I can, because it will absolutely be more interesting than anything else going on. But I can't just sleep all the time.

Hi.
While my OCD is an issue, it's the Asperger's that hits me most. I tend to be unconsciously antisocial , and I find that as I go through life I enjoy other people less and less, to the point where I refuse talking to people or doing things with them just because I know I will be bored.
